notAuthoritativeFor: Code repositories, operations, deployment, or project behavior.

dos: These conventions apply to documentation-only repositories.
donts: Documentation-only repositories must not omit applicable documentation requirements.

dos: Every documentation-only repository must extend the general AGENTS.md requirements with applicable documentation guidance.
donts: A documentation-only repository must not omit AGENTS.md.

dos: After the seven general AGENTS.md headings, add a ## Documentation section. Document documentation scope, authority boundaries, indexes, link validation, and documentation-only limits.
donts: AGENTS.md must not allow implementation code or undocumented authoritative policy in a documentation-only repository.

dos: Documentation-only repositories must provide the required documentation indexes and link each documented surface from the applicable root index.
donts: Documentation-only repositories must not leave required documentation surfaces undiscoverable or introduce implementation code as authoritative policy.

dos: Documentation-only README.md must add Scope, Authority, Navigation, Contribution, and Documentation validation, in that order, for repository scope, authoritative sources, indexes, contribution/setup requirements, and link/document validation. Place these headings in the profile extension area defined by general.json and include them in the Table of Contents.
Documentation-only README.md must link every authoritative documentation surface from its indexes.
donts: Documentation-only README.md must not present implementation code, operational procedures, or duplicated authoritative content.

dos: Deterministic validation must verify that every documented surface, index link, structured-document path, and embedded reference resolves to its intended target.
The Docs authority map must validate repository entries, directive namespaces, structured-document paths, and reciprocal authority references when the referenced checkout is available.
donts: Do not leave a documented path, registry entry, or embedded reference pointing to a missing or unregistered target.
